facts.statement: The only recognized species, Tarbosaurus bataar, is known from the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia and fragmentary remains from the Subashi Formation of China.
facts.quote: It contains the type and single species Tarbosaurus bataar, which is known from the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia, with more fragmentary remains found further afield in the Subashi Formation of China.

facts.statement: The largest Tarbosaurus specimens measured between 10 and 12 meters in length and weighed up to 4.5 to 5 metric tons.
facts.quote: Like most known tyrannosaurids, Tarbosaurus was a large bipedal predator, with the largest specimens measuring 10-12 m and weighing up to 4.5 - 5 MT.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus lived in a humid floodplain environment dominated by deserts, forests, and plains, criss-crossed by river channels.
facts.quote: Tarbosaurus lived in a humid floodplain dominated by deserts, forests, and plains, and criss-crossed by river channels.

facts.statement: As an apex predator, Tarbosaurus preyed on ankylosaurids like Tarchia and Saichania, hadrosaurids like Saurolophus and Barsboldia, and sauropods like Nemegtosaurus and Opisthocoelicaudia.
facts.quote: It was an apex predator in this environment, preying on other large dinosaurs including ankylosaurids, such as Tarchia and Saichania, hadrosaurids, such as Saurolophus and Barsboldia, and sauropods, such as Nemegtosaurus and Opisthocoelicaudia.

facts.statement: A joint Soviet-Mongolian expedition discovered a large theropod skull and vertebrae in the Gobi Desert in 1946.
facts.quote: In 1946, a joint Soviet-Mongolian expedition to the Gobi Desert in the Ömnögovi Province turned up a large theropod skull and some vertebrae from the Nemegt Formation.

facts.statement: The specific name bataar is a misspelling of the Mongolian word for 'hero'.
facts.quote: The specific name is a misspelling of the Mongolian word баатар/baatar, meaning "hero".

facts.statement: In 1965, A. K. Rozhdestvensky proposed that Maleev's specimens represented different growth stages of a single species distinct from North American Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: A 1965 paper by A. K. Rozhdestvensky recognized all of Maleev's specimens as different growth stages of the same species, which he believed to be distinct from the North American Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: In 1992, Ken Carpenter concluded the material belonged to the genus Tyrannosaurus and lumped most specimens into Tyrannosaurus bataar.
facts.quote: American paleontologist Ken Carpenter re-examined the material in 1992. He concluded that it belonged to the genus Tyrannosaurus, as originally published by Maleev, and lumped all the specimens into the species Tyrannosaurus bataar (except the remains that Maleev had named Gorgosaurus novojilovi).

facts.statement: In 1995, Olshevsky, Ford, and Yamamoto created the name Jenghizkhan for T. bataar and recognized three distinct genera from the Nemegt Formation.
facts.quote: George Olshevsky, Tracy Ford and Seiji Yamamoto created the new generic name Jenghizkhan (after Genghis Khan) for Tyrannosaurus bataar in 1995, while also recognizing Tarbosaurus efremovi and Maleevosaurus novojilovi, for a total of three distinct, contemporaneous genera from the Nemegt Formation.

facts.statement: A 1999 study reclassified Maleevosaurus as a juvenile Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: A 1999 study subsequently reclassified Maleevosaurus as a juvenile Tarbosaurus.

facts.statement: Most modern paleontologists recognize only one species, Tarbosaurus bataar, despite many named species in the past.
facts.quote: Although many species have been named, most modern paleontologists recognize only one species, T. bataar.

facts.statement: Some experts consider Tarbosaurus bataar to be an Asian representative of Tyrannosaurus, which would render the genus Tarbosaurus redundant.
facts.quote: Some experts see this species as an Asian representative of the North American genus Tyrannosaurus, which would make the genus Tarbosaurus redundant.

facts.statement: If not synonymous, Tarbosaurus and Tyrannosaurus are considered very closely related genera.
facts.quote: Tarbosaurus and Tyrannosaurus, if not synonymous, are considered to be very closely related genera.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Alioramus is the closest relative of Tarbosaurus, though this view has been disproven by the discovery of Qianzhousaurus and the description of Alioramini.
facts.quote: Alioramus, also from Mongolia, has previously been thought by some authorities to be the closest relative of Tarbosaurus, though this has since been disproven with the discovery of Qianzhousaurus and the description of the tyrannosaurine tribe Alioramini.

facts.statement: Shanshanosaurus huoyanshanensis is provisionally accepted as a synonym of Tarbosaurus bataar by subsequent authors.
facts.quote: Subsequent authors have provisionally accepted S. houyanshanensis as a synonym of Tarbosaurus bataar.

facts.statement: Chingkankousaurus fragilis was once considered a synonym of Tarbosaurus bataar but has since been assessed as a dubious taxon.
facts.quote: Along with Albertosaurus periculosus, Tyrannosaurus luanchuanensis, and Tyrannosaurus "turpanensis," Chingkankousaurus fragilis was considered a provisional junior synonym of Tarbosaurus bataar by Holtz (2004), but it has since been assessed as dubious by Brusatte et al. (2013).

facts.statement: Currie speculated that Alioramus might be a juvenile Tarbosaurus, but noted that its high tooth count and snout crests suggested otherwise.
facts.quote: This led Currie to speculate that Alioramus might represent a juvenile Tarbosaurus, but he noted that the much higher tooth count and row of crests on top of the snout suggested otherwise.

facts.statement: In 1979, Dong Zhiming described teeth, a dorsal vertebra, and fragmentary foot bones of a tyrannosaurid from South China that he tentatively referred to Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1979 Dong Zhiming described several dinosaur remains from the strata of South China, reporting teeth, a dorsal vertebra, and several fragmentary foot bones of a tyrannosaurid.

facts.statement: A Tarbosaurus skeleton returned to Mongolia in 2013 is temporarily displayed on Sukhbaatar Square in Ulaanbaatar.
facts.quote: The dinosaur was returned to Mongolia in 2013, where it is temporarily displayed on Sukhbaatar Square, the center of the city of Ulaanbaatar.

facts.statement: Footprints attributed to Tarbosaurus from the Nemegt locality preserve skin impressions similar to those found on the skin impressions of the Bugiin Tsav skeleton.
facts.quote: The better-preserved track features skin impressions over large areas on and behind the toe impressions that are similar to those discovered in Bugiin Tsav.

facts.statement: A well-preserved Tarbosaurus footprint from the Nemegt locality measures 61 cm in length, indicating it belonged to a large individual.
facts.quote: The track measures 61 cm in length, thus representing a large individual.

facts.statement: The largest known Tarbosaurus skull is approximately 1.35 meters long, making it larger than the skulls of all other tyrannosaurids except Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: The largest known Tarbosaurus skull is about 1.35 m long, which is larger than that of all other tyrannosaurids, aside from Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Between 58 and 64 teeth lined the jaws of Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: Between 58 and 64 teeth lined its jaws.

facts.statement: The longest teeth of Tarbosaurus were located in the upper jaw, with crowns reaching up to 11.2 cm in length.
facts.quote: The longest teeth were in the maxilla (upper jaw bone), with crowns up to 11.2 cm long.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus possessed a unique locking mechanism in the lower jaw where a ridge on the angular bone articulated with the dentary bone, a feature also found in Alioramus.
facts.quote: In the lower jaw, a ridge on the outer surface of the angular bone articulated with the rear of the dentary bone, creating a locking mechanism unique to Tarbosaurus and Alioramus.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus had the smallest arms relative to body size of all tyrannosaurids, with hands containing two clawed digits each.
facts.quote: Tarbosaurus had tiny arms, proportionably to body size the smallest of all members in the family.

facts.statement: The hands of Tarbosaurus had two clawed digits each, with some specimens showing an additional unclawed third metacarpal similar to closely related genera.
facts.quote: The hands had two clawed digits each, with an additional unclawed third metacarpal found in some specimens, similar to those of closely related genera.

facts.statement: Unlike its tiny arms, Tarbosaurus had long, thick, and muscular three-toed legs adapted for supporting its body in a bipedal posture.
facts.quote: In contrast to the arms, the three-toed legs were long, thick, and muscular to support the body in a bipedal posture.

facts.statement: It is debated whether scattered tyrannosaurid remains from the Djadokhta Formation of Mongolia belong to Tarbosaurus, as some researchers consider them dubious or foreign passing taxa.
facts.quote: In 2004, David B. Weishampel and team listed a dubious Tarbosaurus? sp. as a component of the known dinosaur taxa of the Campanian-aged Djadokhta Formation without further ado.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus belongs to the theropod subfamily Tyrannosaurinae within the family Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: Tarbosaurus is classified as a theropod in the subfamily Tyrannosaurinae of the family Tyrannosauridae.

facts.statement: A 2003 study suggested that Alioramus is the closest known relative of Tarbosaurus based on shared skull characteristics.
facts.quote: A 2003 cladistic analysis based on skull features instead identified Alioramus as the closest known relative of Tarbosaurus

facts.statement: A juvenile Tarbosaurus specimen with a 290 mm skull was discovered in 2006 and formally described in 2011.
facts.quote: the 2006 discovery of a juvenile individual (MPC-D 107/7) with a complete, 290 mm long skull was reported and described in 2011

facts.statement: Analysis of sclerotic rings suggests the juvenile Tarbosaurus may have been a crepuscular or nocturnal hunter.
facts.quote: Examination of the sclerotic rings in this juvenile Tarbosaurus suggests they may also have been crepuscular or nocturnal hunters.

facts.statement: A 12-meter-long Tarbosaurus had an estimated total brain volume of 184 cm³.
facts.quote: The total brain volume for a 12 m long Tarbosaurus is estimated at only 184 cm3.

facts.statement: Large olfactory bulbs and nerves indicate that Tarbosaurus possessed a highly keen sense of smell.
facts.quote: The large size of the olfactory bulbs, as well as the terminal and olfactory nerves, suggest that Tarbosaurus had a highly keen sense of smell

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus had a very small midbrain tectum and undeveloped optic and oculomotor nerves, suggesting limited visual processing capabilities.
facts.quote: The midbrain tectum, responsible for visual processing in reptiles, was very small in Tarbosaurus, as were the optic nerve and the oculomotor nerve, which controls eye movement.

facts.statement: Unlike Tyrannosaurus, Tarbosaurus had eyes facing primarily sideways due to a narrower skull, lacking the forward-facing binocular vision of its North American relative.
facts.quote: Unlike Tyrannosaurus, which had forward-facing eyes that provided accurate binocular vision, Tarbosaurus had a narrower skull more typical of other tyrannosaurids in which the eyes faced primarily sideways.

facts.statement: Researchers have debated whether Tarbosaurus relied more on scavenging than active hunting due to its lack of binocular vision, though evidence suggests it actively preyed on large herbivores.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that the lack of binocular vision in Asian tyrannosaurs, like Tarbosaurus, might have been correlated with a greater amount of scavenging resources provided by sauropod carcasses

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus possessed a unique locking mechanism in its lower jaw formed by a ridge on the angular bone articulating with the dentary.
facts.quote: Tarbosaurus had a locking mechanism formed from a ridge on the surface of the angular, which articulated with a square process on the rear of the dentary.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus bataar was originally classified as a species of Tyrannosaurus, a view supported by some recent studies.
facts.quote: Tarbosaurus bataar was originally described as a species of Tyrannosaurus, an arrangement that has been supported by some more recent studies.

facts.statement: While some studies support merging Tarbosaurus into Tyrannosaurus, others prefer to keep them as separate sister genera.
facts.quote: Others prefer to keep the genera separate, while still recognizing them as sister taxa.

facts.statement: A 2005 study revealed that Tarbosaurus had a bite force of 8,000 to 10,000 pounds per square inch, allowing it to crush bones.
facts.quote: As for its bite force, it was revealed in 2005 that Tarbosaurus had a bite force of around 8,000 to 10,000 pounds per square inch of force, meaning that it could crush bones just like its North American relative, Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Stress fractures and tendon avulsions found in Tarbosaurus fossils suggest a very active predation-based diet rather than obligate scavenging.
facts.quote: The presence of stress fractures and tendon avulsions, in general, provide evidence for a "very active" predation-based diet instead of obligate scavenging.

facts.statement: A 2020 stable isotope study found that Tarbosaurus primarily hunted large dinosaurs, specifically titanosaurs and hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: A 2020 study involving stable isotopes found that Tarbosaurus primarily hunted large dinosaurs in its environment, most notably titanosaurs and hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: U-Pb dating suggests Tarbosaurus lived before 66.7 ± 2.5 million years ago during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous, though the exact age remains unresolved.
facts.quote: U-Pb dating from teeth of Tarbosaurus suggested that the deposition of the middle Nemegt Formation happened before 66.7 ± 2.5 Ma, during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous, though whether the depositional age of the formation dates back to the late Campanian remains unresolved.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus lived in the Nemegt Formation, an environment with large river channels and a far more humid climate than surrounding formations.
facts.quote: Tarbosaurus is found chiefly in the Nemegt Formation, whose sediments preserve large river channels and soil deposits that indicate a far more humid climate than those suggested by the underlying Barun Goyot and Djadochta Formations.

facts.statement: The environment where Tarbosaurus lived was semi-arid during certain times of the year.
facts.quote: The area would have been semi-arid during certain times of the year.

facts.statement: As the largest predator in the Nemegt Formation, adult Tarbosaurus likely preyed on large hadrosaurs like Saurolophus and sauropods like Nemegtosaurus.
facts.quote: By far the largest predator known from the formation, adult Tarbosaurus most likely preyed upon large hadrosaurs, such as Saurolophus and Barsboldia, or sauropods, such as Nemegtosaurus and Opisthocoelicaudia.

facts.statement: The genus Tarbosaurus was named by Maleev in 1955.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Maleev, 1955

facts.statement: The species Tarbosaurus bataar was named by Maleev in 1955.
facts.quote: species_authority: Maleev, 1955

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus bataar has numerous synonyms, including Tyrannosaurus bataar, Gorgosaurus novojilovi, and Shanshanosaurus huoyanshanensis.
facts.quote: synonyms: Tyrannosaurus bataar Maleev, 1955 Gorgosaurus novojilovi Maleev, 1955 Tarbosaurus efremovi Maleev, 1955 Gorgosaurus lancinator Maleev, 1955 Deinodon novojilovi (Maleev, 1955) Deinodon lancinator (Maleev, 1955) Aublysodon lancinator (Maleev, 1955) Charig, 1967 Aublysodon novojilovi (Maleev, 1955) Charig, 1967 Shanshanosaurus huoyanshanensis Dong, 1977 Tyrannosaurus efremovi (Maleev, 1955) Tarbosaurus novojilovi (Maleev, 1955) Aublysodon huoyanshanensis (Dong, 1977) Albertosaurus novojilovi (Maleev, 1955) Maleevosaurus novojilovi (Maleev, 1955) Jenghizkhan bataar (Maleev, 1955) Tyrannosaurus novojilovi (Maleev, 1955) ?Raptorex kriegsteini Sereno et al., 2009

facts.statement: In 2011, David W. E. Hone and Mahito Watabe reported bite marks on a Saurolophus humerus attributed to Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: David W. E. Hone and Mahito Watabe in 2011 reported the left humerus of a nearly complete Saurolophus skeleton (MPC-D 100/764) from the Bügiin Tsav locality of the Nemegt Formation, which was heavily damaged from bite marks attributed to Tarbosaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Tarbosaurus bite marks on Deinocheirus represent feeding behavior focused on internal organs rather than aggression.
facts.quote: The bite marks probably represent feeding behavior instead of aggression between the species and the fact that bite marks were not found elsewhere on the body indicates the predator focused on internal organs.

facts.statement: It remains unresolved whether the depositional age of the Nemegt Formation dates back to the late Campanian.
facts.quote: though whether the depositional age of the formation dates back to the late Campanian remains unresolved.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus bataar is the only known species in the genus Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: Tarbosaurus bataar es la única especie conocida del género Tarbosaurus

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 70.6 to 68.5 million years ago in the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 70,6 y 68,5 millones, en el Maastrichtiense

facts.statement: Fossils of Tarbosaurus have been recovered in Mongolia and fragmentary remains found in parts of China.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Asia. Los fósiles se han recuperado en Mongolia, con más restos fragmentarios encontrados muy lejos, en partes de China.

facts.statement: Modern paleontologists recognize only one species, Tarbosaurus bataar, as valid despite many named species.
facts.quote: Aunque se hayan nombrado muchas especies, los paleontólogos modernos reconocen solamente una, Tarbosaurus bataar, como válido.

facts.statement: Some experts suggest Tarbosaurus bataar is actually an Asian representative of the North American genus Tyrannosaurus, which would invalidate the genus Tarbosaurus if true.
facts.quote: Algunos expertos afirman que esta especie es realmente un representante asiático del género norteamericano Tyrannosaurus, si es cierto, esto invalidaría el género Tarbosaurus en conjunto.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus and Tyrannosaurus are considered closely related genera, even if they are not synonyms.
facts.quote: Tarbosaurus y Tyrannosaurus se consideran géneros estrechamente vinculados, incluso si no son sinónimos.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus was a large, bipedal carnivore weighing more than one ton and equipped with dozens of large, sharp teeth.
facts.quote: Como la mayoría de los tiranosáuridos conocidos, Tarbosaurus era un carnívoro bípedo grande, pesando más de una tonelada y equipado de docenas de grandes y agudos dientes.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus measured approximately 10 meters in length, 3 meters in hip height, and weighed up to 4.5 metric tons.
facts.quote: Medía aproximadamente 10 metros de largo, 3 de altura de la cadera y pesaba hasta 4,5 toneladas métricas de masa corporal.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus had a unique locking mechanism in its lower jaw and possessed disproportionately tiny two-fingered arms, the smallest relative to body size of all tyrannosaurids.
facts.quote: Tuvo un mecanismo de bloqueo único en su mandíbula inferior y el tamaño de los miembros superiores en relación con del cuerpo es el más pequeño de todos los tiránosauridos, con desproporcionados minúsculos brazos, de solo dos dedos.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus lived in a humid alluvial terrain cut by river channels.
facts.quote: Tarbosaurus vivió en un terreno aluvional húmedo surcado por los canales de ríos.

facts.statement: In its environment, Tarbosaurus was the apex predator, likely hunting large dinosaurs such as the hadrosaurid Saurolophus or the sauropod Nemegtosaurus.
facts.quote: En este ambiente, era el superpredador en el extremo de la cadena alimentaria, cazando probablemente en otros dinosaurios grandes como el hadrosáurido Saurolophus o el saurópodo Nemegtosaurus.

facts.statement: Although smaller than Tyrannosaurus, Tarbosaurus was one of the largest tyrannosaurids, with fully developed individuals reaching 10 to 12 meters in length, 3 meters in hip height, and weighing up to 4.3 to 4.5 tons.
facts.quote: Aunque más pequeño que Tyrannosaurus, Tarbosaurus era uno de los tiranosáuridos más grandes, con el individuo completamente desarrollado más grande que medía aproximadamente entre 10 a 12 metros de largo, 3 de altura de la cadera y pesaba hasta 4,3 a 4,5 toneladas en masa corporal

facts.statement: The longest Tarbosaurus skull is over 1.3 meters long, longer than other tyrannosaurids except Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: El cráneo más largo de Tarbosaurus es de más de 1,3 metros de largo, más que los otros tiranosáuridos excepto Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: The lack of posterior skull expansion in Tarbosaurus means its eyes did not look directly forward, suggesting it lacked the same binocular field of vision as Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: La falta de expansión de la parte trasera del cráneo de Tarbosaurus hace que los ojos no miren directamente hacia adelante, sugiriendo que no poseía el mismo campo de visión binocular de Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Between 60 and 64 teeth were aligned in Tarbosaurus jaws, slightly more than in Tyrannosaurus but fewer than in small tyrannosaurids like Gorgosaurus and Alioramus.
facts.quote: Entre 60 y 64 dientes se alineaban en sus mandíbulas, ligeramente más que en Tyrannosaurus pero menos que en los pequeños tiranosáuridos como Gorgosaurus y Alioramus.

facts.statement: The longest tooth in Tarbosaurus was in the maxilla, with a crown measuring more than 85 millimeters.
facts.quote: El diente más largo se encontraba en el maxilar, hueso que forma la mayor parte de la quijada superior que tenía una corona de más de 85 milímetros.

facts.statement: In the lower jaw, a border of the external surface of the angular bone articulates with the posterior of the dentary, creating a lower jaw locking mechanism seen only in Tarbosaurus and Alioramus.
facts.quote: En la mandíbula inferior, un borde de la superficie externa del hueso angular articula con la parte posterior del dentario, creando un mecanismo de trabado de la mandíbula inferior únicamente visto en Tarbosaurus y Alioramus.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus had minute forelimbs with two fingers, which were smaller relative to body size than any other member of its family.
facts.quote: Tarbosaurus tenía miembros anteriores minúsculos, con dos dedos, que eran más pequeños en comparación a su tamaño de cuerpo que los de cualquier otro miembro de su familia.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus hands had two fingers with claws each, with an additional clawless third metacarpal found in some specimens, similar to closely related genera.
facts.quote: Las manos tenían dos dedos con garras cada una, con un tercer metacarpiano adicional sin garras encontrado en algunos especímenes, similar a géneros estrechamente relacionados.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus had long, thick hind legs that walked on the tips of three toes, maintaining a bipedal posture.
facts.quote: Los miembros posteriores que pisaban con la punta de los tres dedos del pie eran largos y gruesos, manteniendo el cuerpo en una postura bípeda.

facts.statement: The long, heavy tail served as a counterbalance to the head and torso and positioned the center of gravity over the hips.
facts.quote: La cola, larga y pesada sirvió como contrapeso a la cabeza y al torso y colocaba el centro de gravedad sobre las caderas.

facts.statement: A $1 million smuggling deal was discovered when suspicions arose about a Heritage Auctions catalog for a New York event on May 20, 2012.
facts.quote: Se descubrió un trato de contrabando de $ 1 millón cuando se levantaron sospechas sobre un catálogo publicado por Heritage Auctions para un evento en la ciudad de Nueva York el 20 de mayo de 2012.

facts.statement: Smuggler Eric Prokopi pleaded guilty to illegal smuggling, and the dinosaur was returned to Mongolia in 2013, where it was temporarily exhibited in Sükhbaatar Square in Ulaanbaatar.
facts.quote: Eric Prokopi, el contrabandista, se declaró culpable de contrabando ilegal y el dinosaurio fue devuelto a Mongolia en 2013, donde se exhibe temporalmente en la Plaza Sükhbaatar, el centro de la ciudad de Ulán Bator.

facts.statement: The case led to the repatriation of dozens more Mongolian dinosaurs, including several Tarbosaurus bataar skeletons.
facts.quote: El caso condujo a la repatriación de docenas más de dinosaurios mongoles, incluidos varios esqueletos de Tarbosaurus bataar.

facts.statement: Skin impressions from a large Tarbosaurus skeleton found at Bugiin Tsav were later destroyed by poachers.
facts.quote: Se recuperaron impresiones de piel de un gran esqueleto en la localidad de Bugiin Tsav que posteriormente fue destruido por cazadores furtivos.

facts.statement: A preserved Tarbosaurus footprint measures 61 centimeters in length, representing a large individual.
facts.quote: La pista mide 61 centímetros de largo, lo que representa a un individuo grande.

facts.statement: Researchers speculated that the Tarbosaurus throat pouch may have been used for display, possibly being brightly colored and inflatable like a frigatebird's pouch.
facts.quote: Carpenter especuló que la bolsa pudo haber sido utilizada para exhibición, posiblemente siendo de colores brillantes e inflable como la de un pájaro fragata.

facts.statement: The Tarbosaurus skull with throat pouch impressions may be the same specimen supposedly destroyed by poachers in 1992.
facts.quote: Este espécimen puede ser el mismo que supuestamente fue destruido por cazadores furtivos en 1992.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus belongs to the subfamily Tyrannosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tyrannosaurini

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus is classified within the family Tyrannosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Tyrannosauridae

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus lived from the Coniacian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 89.8 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Maastrichtian (89.8 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: About one-quarter of all fossils collected from the Nemegt Formation belong to Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: De hecho, un cuarto de todos los fósiles recogidos de la Formación Nemegt pertenece a Tarbosaurus.

facts.statement: The total brain volume for a 12-meter Tarbosaurus is estimated at only 184 cubic centimeters.
facts.quote: El volumen encefálico total para un tarbosaurio de 12 metros se estima en solo 184 centímetros cúbicos.

facts.statement: The large olfactory bulb and associated nerves suggest Tarbosaurus had a keen sense of smell, similar to Tyrannosaurus.
facts.quote: El gran tamaño del bulbo olfativo, así como el nervio terminal y nervio olfativo, sugieren que Tarbosaurus tenía un afinado sentido del olfato, al igual que Tyrannosaurus.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus had a large vomeronasal organ used for detecting pheromones, suggesting complex mating behavior.
facts.quote: El bulbo vomeronasal es grande y diferenciado del bulbo olfatorio, indicando un bien desarrollado órgano de Jacobson, que era utilizado para detectar feromonas.

facts.statement: Tarbosaurus had a large auditory nerve suggesting a good sense of hearing useful for communication and spatial awareness.
facts.quote: El nervio auditivo era también grande, sugiriendo un buen sentido del oído, que pudo haber sido útil la comunicación y conocimiento espacial.

facts.statement: Nerves and brain structures associated with vision were smaller and underdeveloped in Tarbosaurus.
facts.quote: En cambio, los nervios y las estructuras del cerebro asociados a la vista eran más pequeños y subdesarrollados.

facts.statement: Unlike Tyrannosaurus, Tarbosaurus had eyes placed mostly on the sides of a narrower skull, lacking significant binocular vision.
facts.quote: A diferencia de Tyrannosaurus, que tenía ojos hacia adelante lo que proporcionaron un cierto grado de visión binocular, Tarbosaurus tenía un cráneo más estrecho más típico de otros tiranosáuridos en los cuales los ojos se colocaron sobre todo de lado.

facts.statement: Some researchers, such as Carr et al., have invalidated the species name Tarbosaurus bataar, suggesting it is a synonym of Tyrannosaurus bataar.
facts.quote: Nota: Carr et al. validan Tyrannosaurus bataar e invalidan Tarbosaurus bataar

facts.statement: A 2026 study suggests that the fossils of Asiatyrannus xui and Raptorex kriegsteini are likely juvenile specimens of Tarbosaurus bataar.
facts.quote: Raun et al. (2026) revise proposed diagnostic characters of Asiatyrannus xui and Raptorex kriegsteini, and interpret the type material of both taxa as likely to be juvenile specimens of Tarbosaurus bataar.

rejected.statement: Tarbosaurus is a genus of large tyrannosaurid dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period.
rejected.quote: Tarbosaurus ( ; meaning "alarming lizard") is a genus of large tyrannosaurid dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is a genus of large tyrannosaurid dinosaur that'

rejected.statement: Tarbosaurus possessed a unique jaw locking mechanism, about sixty large teeth, and the smallest arms relative to body size among tyrannosaurids, featuring tiny two-fingered hands.
rejected.quote: It had a unique locking mechanism in its jaw, equipped with about sixty large teeth, and the smallest arms relative to body size of all tyrannosaurids, renowned for their disproportionately tiny, two-fingered hands.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'about sixty large teeth and the smallest arms'

rejected.statement: Soviet paleontologist Evgeny Maleev named the 1946 specimen Tyrannosaurus bataar in 1955.
rejected.quote: In 1955, Evgeny Maleev, a Soviet paleontologist, made this specimen the holotype (PIN 551–1) of a new species, which he called Tyrannosaurus bataar.
rejected.reason: numbers not in the quote: ['1946']
